name: optional-isa-sample-three
purpose: Exploratory three-arm mechanism sample: official control, optional LibreCalc hybrid, and compulsory LibreCalc. One task per non-visual category, drawn from the already-measured deterministic control slice. This sample is development data and cannot support a performance claim; it only tests whether the semantic primitives add capability when the model retains bash/openpyxl.
sampling: The middle task by sorted position within each category of control-arm-fifteen: Template:10_02, Financial_Model:13_02, Debugging:06_09. Selection is deterministic but outcomes are already known, so the sample is diagnostic rather than held-out.

arms.A_control: Official SpreadsheetBench 2 bash + view_xlsx + openpyxl prompt and tools.
arms.H_hybrid: Officially general programming plus category-specific LibreCalc observations, all deterministic LibreCalc writes, and calc_compare; LibreCalc use is optional.
arms.S_strict: Category-specific LibreCalc configuration with bash/view_xlsx absent; reads unbounded so known refusal failures do not confound compulsory-ISA cost.

success_reading.hybrid_beats_control: LibreCalc adds useful capability when optional.
success_reading.hybrid_beats_strict: Compulsory loss of general programming is part of the current deficit.
success_reading.hybrid_matches_control_but_is_cheaper: The defensible benefit is efficiency, subject to quality non-inferiority in a larger run.
success_reading.hybrid_does_not_help: The current primitives or their presentation do not add measurable end-to-end value on this sample.
